FY26 guide reaffirmed in August: revenue $140-190M, adj. EBITDA $10-15M (tracking the high end), OCF $0-10M, year-end ARR $65-70M; H1 OCF was -$8.0M. Events in the price: NYSE 802.01B notice (market cap and equity under $50M, filed 2026-10-23; the 30-day average cap is now about $29.5M against the $15M floor that would end the cure period), a strategic review announced 2026-10-26 with Guggenheim, Gibson Dunn and Davis Polk and 'refinancing, recapitalization' listed among the options (-13% that week), and the release moved from Nov 5 to today, the 10-Q deadline, for 'scheduling and logistical reasons' (stock +21.5% intraday on 1.8M shares on Nov 4, then -24% on Nov 5). Short interest about 12% of float, about 11 days to cover (aggregators, late September).
view: The price is no longer set by the operating line. At about $19M of equity under roughly $320M of debt, the stock trades as an option on what the strategic review leaves the shareholders. Q2 beat and reaffirmed (+14.5% the next day). The stock then lost two thirds of its value with no operating news: an NYSE notice that was mechanical on the price, and a review whose advisers and listed options (recap, refinancing) read as balance-sheet work. So tonight turns on three things: whether guidance is reaffirmed or withdrawn, whether cash held near $38M (the OCF guide needs a positive H2), and what the release and call say about the review. The results alone could easily produce a relief bounce off a 52-week low with a 12% short base and thin volume. Withdrawn guidance, a cash step-down, impairments or going-concern language, or a recap framed as the review's direction, would take it lower. A transaction announced with the results is possible but not the base case: the company said it would not update until a deal was approved, and it kept an ordinary 17:00 call. Even a sale may leave equity little at this enterprise value. The delay to the deadline weighs slightly negative, but it is not evidence. I cannot tell which way the release lands. The move will be large either way.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is what the release says about the review and the balance sheet (guide kept or withdrawn, cash, any substantial-doubt language). None of that is visible beforehand, and the inputs point both ways. A 68% fall since a print that beat and reaffirmed, a 12% short base and thin volume favour a relief move on ordinary numbers. A delay to the filing deadline, restructuring-style advisers and $320M of debt against a $19M equity favour a bad surprise. Nothing reaches 65% either way.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Short side: guidance withdrawn plus a cash step-down or going-concern language in the 10-Q. Long side: FY26 EBITDA/OCF guide reaffirmed with cash at or above $38M and no change to the review's framing.

self_critique: The case for the downside is stronger than 46 implies. A company with restructuring counsel, $320M of debt and a $19M equity moved its print to the filing deadline. That pattern often comes with withdrawn guidance, impairments or recap language, and the -28% in the last week may be informed selling. The case for the upside: a 12% short base with 11 days to cover, a stock down 68% since a print that beat and reaffirmed, and any reaffirmation could squeeze it 20-30%. These two cases cancel. That is why there is no call.
approach_notes: P6 helped most: splitting the run-in showed the price is set by the capital structure, not the operating line. P4/P7 did not help much here, because the deciding line (the review and the guide) has no visible inputs before the release; a note on equity priced as an option on distressed debt would help.
